question: Will the CDC's measles data page show at least one confirmed 2026 U.S. measles death as of October 1, 2026?

calls.reasoning: Status quo is the asterisk, and the CDC has explicitly gated the cell on NCHS underlying-cause death records rather than state reports. Of the four Pennsylvania measles-associated deaths, the Aug 14 newborn was certified with a traumatic splenic laceration as the cause (measles only in Part II), so it cannot generate a qualifying record; the 6-week-old (coroner: measles, with Amish lethal microcephaly as a comorbidity that could itself be coded underlying) had still produced no NCHS record as of Sept 18, ~2 weeks after RFK Jr. publicly accepted the coroner's finding; the 18-year-old and 40-year-old died ~Sept 12-15, inside the 1-8 week certificate-to-NCHS-coding lag. Only one scheduled page update (Fri Sept 25) falls before the 23:59 ET Oct 1 observation, and CDC leadership has already demonstrated willingness to delay publication under review. A methodology reversal via the CSTE standardized-definition work is unlikely to land inside 10 days. The residual YES mass covers a September death being coded fast plus an ad hoc page edit under political pressure.
sources: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK618498/ (NCHS Vital Statistics Rapid Release: Timeliness of Death Certificate Data, 2023)

calls.reconciliation: No web access this run; reconciled on the dossiers. Disputes: (1) update cadence - Friday-publication (Runs 1/3) is better supported than Wednesday (Runs 2/4) because the page's own Sept 18 stamp carries Sept 17 data, i.e. the Wednesday date is the cutoff, not the publication; immaterial either way since 1-2 slots plus precedented off-cycle edits remain. (2) Jefferson Co. certificate wording - Run 2's 'amended 9/14 to probable measles in Part I' and Runs 3/4's 'respiratory failure due to measles complications' are compatible; this is the live YES path, discounted for re-filing delay and ACME competition with COPD/asthma. (3) Second Lancaster infant's underlying cause - unsettleable, no run located the certificate; it carries genuine uncertainty, partly offset by the Sept 18 footnote showing no record at ~5 weeks. (4) Window-elapsed 72% vs 96% is a framing artifact (accrual year vs question window); binding quantity is ~10.6 days. (5) CDC's NCHS pull cadence - unknown to all runs, and unknown latency can only push toward NO. I adopt Run 4's reference class (contested federal statistic, ~0.12-0.15 prior) but land below all four runs: each priced the NCHS lag well, none fully priced the conjunction of lag AND underlying-cause selection against real competing causes AND unknown pull cadence AND discretionary publication by an actor that already removed these deaths once.

disagreements.claim: CDC publishes the measles page on Fridays (Sept 25 the only pre-deadline slot) vs Wednesdays (Sept 23 and Sept 30)
disagreements.verdict: Friday publication favored - the page's Sept 18 last-updated stamp carries Sept 17 'as of' data, so Wednesday is the data cutoff. Immaterial: both readings leave 1-2 slots and off-cycle edits have August precedent.

disagreements.claim: The Jefferson County certificate lists measles in Part I
disagreements.verdict: Run 2's 'probable measles' amendment (Sept 14) and Runs 3/4's 'respiratory failure due to measles complications' are consistent; accepted as the strongest YES path, but discounted for amendment re-filing and COPD/asthma competing in underlying-cause selection.

disagreements.claim: The second Lancaster infant could yield a measles-underlying-cause NCHS record
disagreements.verdict: Unsettleable from the dossiers - no run found the certificate wording. Left uncertain; the Sept 18 footnote (no qualifying record at ~5 weeks post-death) is the only direct evidence and points NO.

disagreements.claim: Share of the question window elapsed: ~72% (Run 1) vs ~96% (Runs 2/3)
disagreements.verdict: Artifact of measuring the calendar-2026 accrual year versus the question window. Neither is wrong on its own terms; the decision-relevant quantity is ~10.6 days to the observation instant.

disagreements.claim: How often CDC pulls the NCHS file for this page
disagreements.verdict: Not established by any run. Treated as an additional, asymmetric source of latency favoring NO rather than assumed to be weekly.

disagreements.claim: How much weight the acute political pressure (Shapiro, Epi-Aid, press, CSTE) deserves as a YES driver
disagreements.verdict: No evidence breaks this tie. I take the reading that pressure has so far produced only movement away from displaying deaths - the NCHS rule was adopted after RFK Jr. accepted a coroner's measles finding - so I weight it low.

calls.reference_class: Contested federal data cells whose publication rule was set by leadership to exclude the disputed events, observed over a ~10-day window with 1-2 scheduled refreshes; cross-checked against NCHS death-to-provisional-record timeliness for coroner-certified deaths 2-3 weeks old
